By Kat Boboris · October 1 st 2026

arXiv, and the scientific community at large, are facing a watershed moment. Scholarly publishing is currently changing at a rapid pace, and we are seeing a massive transformation in how researchers communicate their results.

Before the advent of AI, there was an easily discernible, practical limit to the rate at which independent submissions could be produced, and arXiv’s volunteer moderators would limit submitters who were well above that threshold. With AI tools becoming more advanced and accessible to authors, the “practical limit” of how many papers can be submitted is now up for debate. As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap while we determine what may be the new best practice for authors employing more and more advanced AI tools, and to give us time to improve our moderation tools and procedures accordingly.

Open access repositories across the board are seeing a sharp increase in the number of submissions per author, per month. In September of 2016, arXiv received 9,869 submissions. In September of 2024, arXiv received 20,569 submissions. This September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions, which in turn generated almost 9,000 support tickets for arXiv staff and moderators. In only the past two years, submissions have doubled.

Advanced AI tools are helping drive these increases by making certain aspects of research faster and easier. arXiv policy permits authors to employ AI as a tool in support of their research as long as it is disclosed and the research meets arXiv’s standards of scholarly interest and advances the field of research. However, many of the submissions that arXiv is now receiving do not satisfy these requirements. Our moderators are observing an increase in thin papers of narrow scope, as well as ‘salami’ papers, where a single work is broken up and submitted as a set of smaller papers. There is also a marked increase in dense, AI-written papers. AI tools are making it easy for authors to flood arXiv and other repositories with these low-value papers.

The heart of arXiv’s process for detecting and rejecting low-quality papers is our many volunteer moderators. We are so grateful that they donate their time and expertise every day. However, a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time. This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.

arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time. This policy update is being put into effect to equitably distribute our volunteer moderators’ time across arXiv authors, and protect the arXiv corpus from a sharp increase in inappropriate submissions.

Rate-limiting is an established arXiv policy, with limiting originally primarily left to moderator discretion. arXiv has always asked that authors follow our codes of conduct and our submission guidelines. Articles submitted to arXiv must be of original, novel, and significant self-contained research that is relevant to arXiv categories. All submissions to arXiv must meet prescribed scholarly standards and be of scholarly interest to the scientific community. This policy update strives to fairly distribute the incredibly valuable work of our volunteer moderators who check that submissions meet these standards, and we hope it will also encourage authors to curate and submit only their best work to arXiv.

Thank you to our scientific community for supporting us in this policy update. We rely on you to help us keep arXiv open, fast, and free, and to help us make sure submissions to arXiv are scientifically rigorous, of interest to the community, and in keeping with current academic standards.

As with all policies, we will continue to monitor the effect of this update on authors, readers, and the arXiv corpus, and modify as needed. Our goal in policy updates is to not only protect arXiv’s corpus, but to improve the arXiv experience for everyone who makes arXiv possible – authors, readers, staff, and all our volunteer moderators.
chineseTitle: ArXiv 更新的速率限制政策
chineseContent:
作者：凯特·博波里斯·2026 年 10 月 1 日

arXiv 以及整个科学界正面临着一个分水岭。学术出版目前正在快速变化，我们看到研究人员交流结果的方式发生了巨大转变。

在人工智能出现之前，独立提交的生成速度存在一个易于辨别的实际限制，而 arXiv 的志愿者版主将限制远高于该阈值的提交者。随着人工智能工具变得更加先进且可供作者使用，可以提交的论文数量的“实际限制”现在引起了争论。自 2026 年 10 月 1 日起，arXiv 将对所有提交者和类别制定更新的速率限制政策，作为权宜之计，同时我们确定对于使用越来越先进的人工智能工具的作者来说可能是新的最佳实践，并让我们有时间相应地改进我们的审核工具和程序。

全面开放获取存储库的每个作者每月提交的数量急剧增加。 2016 年 9 月，arXiv 收到了 9,869 份提交内容。 2024 年 9 月，arXiv 收到了 20,569 份提交内容。今年 9 月，arXiv 收到了 40,363 份提交，这反过来又为 arXiv 工作人员和版主带来了近 9,000 张支持票。仅在过去两年，提交的材料就增加了一倍。

先进的人工智能工具使某些方面的研究变得更快、更容易，从而帮助推动这些增长。 arXiv 政策允许作者使用人工智能作为支持其研究的工具，只要人工智能被公开并且研究符合 arXiv 的学术兴趣标准并推动研究领域发展。然而，arXiv 现在收到的许多提交内容都不满足这些要求。我们的版主观察到范围狭窄的薄论文以及“萨拉米”论文的增加，其中单个作品被分解并作为一组较小的论文提交。由人工智能撰写的密集论文也显着增加。人工智能工具使作者可以轻松地将这些低价值论文充斥到 arXiv 和其他存储库中。

arXiv 检测和拒绝低质量论文流程的核心是我们众多的志愿者版主。我们非常感谢他们每天贡献自己的时间和专业知识。然而，相对较小比例的作者提交了大量低质量的论文，并占用了版主不成比例的时间。这对于继续提交高质量论文的作者来说是不公平的——他们的论文可能因此被推迟数天或数周。

arXiv 现在限制提交者每个日历月最多提交两次，任何给定时间的活跃提交总数限制为三个。此次政策更新的实施是为了在 arXiv 作者之间公平分配志愿者版主的时间，并保护 arXiv 语料库免受不当提交急剧增加的影响。

速率限制是一项既定的 arXiv 政策，最初的限制主要由版主自行决定。 arXiv 始终要求作者遵守我们的行为准则和提交指南。提交给 arXiv 的文章必须是与 arXiv 类别相关的原创、新颖且重要的独立研究。所有向 arXiv 提交的内容都必须符合规定的学术标准，并且对科学界具有学术兴趣。此政策更新致力于公平分配我们的志愿者版主的极其有价值的作品，他们检查提交的内容是否符合这些标准，我们希望它也能鼓励作者策划并只向 arXiv 提交他们最好的作品。

感谢我们的科学界对本次政策更新的支持。我们依靠您来帮助我们保持 arXiv 的开放、快速和免费，并帮助我们确保向 arXiv 提交的内容具有科学严谨性、符合社区的利益并符合当前的学术标准。

与所有政策一样，我们将继续监控本次更新对作者、读者和 arXiv 语料库的影响，并根据需要进行修改。我们政策更新的目标不仅是保护 arXiv 的语料库，而且是为所有使 arXiv 成为可能的人（作者、读者、工作人员和我们所有的志愿者版主）改善 arXiv 体验。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
